claims.claim_text: A data analytics company deployed a 40-node bare-metal Kubernetes cluster with local SATA SSDs.
claims.anchor_text: A data analytics company deployed a 40-node Kubernetes cluster on bare metal with local SATA SSDs in each server.
claims.suggested_rewrite: A team can deploy Kubernetes on bare metal with only local SSDs in each server and later discover that stateful workloads need storage that survives node rescheduling.
claims.rationale: This is an unattributed war story with a precise cluster size and storage configuration.

claims.claim_text: The cluster worked for the first six months.
claims.anchor_text: For the first six months, everything worked.
claims.suggested_rewrite: For a while, everything can appear to work.
claims.rationale: The six-month timeline is fake precision without a cited incident source.

claims.claim_text: After a worker failure, Kafka lost 4 hours of event data and required 3 days of manual partition rebalancing.
claims.anchor_text: When a worker node failed, Kafka brokers were rescheduled to new nodes — but their data was on the dead node's local SSDs. They lost 4 hours of event data and spent 3 days manually rebalancing partitions.
claims.suggested_rewrite: When a worker node failed, brokers could be rescheduled elsewhere while their local data remained unavailable, turning a node failure into an extended recovery exercise.
claims.rationale: The event loss and recovery duration are precise incident details with no attribution.

claims.claim_text: Deploying Ceph via Rook on the same SSDs caused a 60% performance drop.
claims.anchor_text: They then deployed Ceph via Rook on the same SSDs. Performance dropped 60%.
claims.suggested_rewrite: They then tried adding Ceph via Rook on the same SSDs, which can create a new contention path instead of solving the original architecture problem.
claims.rationale: The 60% performance drop is an unattributed benchmark from a fabricated or composite anecdote.

claims.claim_text: Ceph replication tripled write load in the anecdotal deployment.
claims.rationale: Ceph documentation explains the common three-replica pool configuration that creates three stored copies.

claims.claim_text: Ceph rebalancing consumed 80% of cluster I/O bandwidth for 4 hours after a node failure.
claims.anchor_text: Their monitoring showed that Ceph rebalancing after a node failure consumed 80% of cluster I/O bandwidth for 4 hours, making all applications sluggish.
claims.suggested_rewrite: Ceph rebalancing after a node failure can consume substantial shared I/O bandwidth, making unrelated applications sluggish.
claims.rationale: The bandwidth percentage and duration are precise incident metrics without a source.

claims.claim_text: The fix dedicated 6 Ceph OSD servers with NVMe drives and a dedicated VLAN with jumbo frames.
claims.anchor_text: The fix was dedicating 6 servers as Ceph OSD nodes with NVMe drives, separated from the Kubernetes worker nodes.
claims.suggested_rewrite: The fix was to separate Ceph OSD capacity from general worker capacity and size the storage tier explicitly.
claims.rationale: The exact remediation size is part of the unattributed war story.

claims.claim_text: Storage traffic in the anecdote ran on a dedicated VLAN with jumbo frames.
claims.anchor_text: Storage traffic ran on a dedicated VLAN with jumbo frames.
claims.suggested_rewrite: Storage traffic should be isolated from application traffic when shared network bandwidth becomes a bottleneck.
claims.rationale: This is an unattributed remediation detail from the same anecdote.

claims.claim_text: The Container Storage Interface spec is currently at v1.12.0.
claims.rationale: The CSI GitHub release page directly identifies v1.12.0.

claims.claim_text: Kubernetes CSI support graduated to GA in v1.13.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes blog announcement states CSI was promoted to GA in v1.13.

claims.claim_text: CephFS and RBD in-tree PersistentVolume plugins are not available starting in Kubernetes v1.31, and FlexVolume is deprecated.
claims.rationale: The PersistentVolumes documentation lists cephfs and rbd as unavailable starting v1.31 and FlexVolume as deprecated.

claims.claim_text: ReadWriteOncePod is stable in Kubernetes v1.29 and constrains a PVC to one pod cluster-wide.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes PersistentVolumes documentation gives RWOP's v1.29 stable status and semantics.

claims.claim_text: StorageClass volumeBindingMode defaults to Immediate, and WaitForFirstConsumer delays binding/provisioning for topology-aware scheduling.
claims.rationale: The StorageClass documentation directly explains Immediate and WaitForFirstConsumer behavior.

claims.claim_text: PersistentVolume volumeMode supports Filesystem and Block, with Filesystem as the default, and Block stable since v1.18.
claims.rationale: The PersistentVolumes documentation states both modes, default Filesystem behavior, and v1.18 stable status.

claims.claim_text: Storage Object in Use Protection prevents deletion of PVCs and PVs that are bound or in use.
claims.rationale: The PersistentVolumes documentation includes the Storage Object in Use Protection behavior.

claims.claim_text: Dynamically provisioned PersistentVolumes inherit the StorageClass reclaim policy, which defaults to Delete; Retain is also supported.
claims.rationale: The StorageClass documentation states the Delete default and Retain/Delete options.

claims.claim_text: PersistentVolumeClaim expansion for CSI volumes is stable in Kubernetes v1.24.
claims.rationale: The PersistentVolumes documentation marks PVC expansion stable in v1.24.

claims.claim_text: CSI Storage Capacity Tracking is stable in Kubernetes v1.24.
claims.rationale: The Storage Capacity documentation marks the feature as Kubernetes v1.24 stable.

claims.claim_text: Generic Ephemeral Volumes are stable in Kubernetes v1.23.
claims.rationale: The Ephemeral Volumes documentation marks generic ephemeral volumes stable in v1.23.

claims.claim_text: Volume Snapshots are GA in Kubernetes v1.20.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes announcement states Volume Snapshot moved to GA in v1.20.

claims.claim_text: Volume Populators graduated to GA in Kubernetes v1.33.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes v1.33 blog post announces Volume Populators GA.

claims.claim_text: VolumeAttributesClass graduated to GA in Kubernetes v1.34.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes v1.34 blog post announces VolumeAttributesClass GA.

claims.claim_text: OCI image volumes are GA in Kubernetes v1.35.
claims.anchor_text: OCI image volumes (GA in v1.35)
claims.suggested_rewrite: OCI image volumes (check the feature state for your Kubernetes release)
claims.rationale: Kubernetes documentation marks image volumes as beta in v1.35, so the GA claim is false.

claims.claim_text: Volume Group Snapshots were alpha in v1.27, beta in v1.32, second beta in v1.34, and GA in v1.36.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes v1.36 announcement gives the feature's alpha, beta, second beta, and GA timeline.

claims.claim_text: CSI Volume Health Monitoring is alpha.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes Volume Health Monitoring page marks the feature as alpha.

claims.claim_text: The core CSI migration framework reached GA in Kubernetes v1.25.
claims.rationale: The Kubernetes v1.25 CSI migration status update states the core migration framework is GA.

claims.claim_text: Legacy cloud plugins for AWS EBS were removed entirely, with unverified sources pointing to v1.27.
claims.anchor_text: Note that legacy cloud plugins for AWS EBS were removed entirely (unverified sources point to v1.27, but the specific removal release lacks official changelog confirmation).
claims.suggested_rewrite: Note that legacy in-tree storage plugins have been steadily migrated or removed; check the current PersistentVolume documentation before relying on an in-tree plugin.
claims.rationale: The sentence admits the release detail is unverified and live Kubernetes docs do not support the AWS EBS removal claim as written.

claims.claim_text: The Recycle reclaim policy is fully deprecated and unsupported by CSI, with a rumored v1.11 deprecation.
claims.anchor_text: The `Recycle` reclaim policy is fully deprecated and unsupported by CSI (GitHub issue #59060 confirms deprecation, though the exact version—rumored to be v1.11—remains unverified in authoritative release notes).
claims.suggested_rewrite: The `Recycle` reclaim policy is deprecated; use dynamic provisioning with `Delete` or `Retain` reclaim policy instead.
claims.rationale: The policy deprecation is real, but the GitHub issue and rumored release detail should not remain as uncited specifics.

claims.claim_text: etcd requires p99 fsync latency below 10ms.
claims.rationale: The etcd FAQ is the authoritative source for the p99 WAL fsync threshold, but etcd.io is not allowlisted.

claims.claim_text: Kafka replicates data.
claims.rationale: The Apache Kafka documentation directly describes Kafka replication.

claims.claim_text: NVMe Gen5 storage provides 1M+ IOPS, sub-100μs latency, and costs $300/TB.
claims.anchor_text: | **0** | NVMe Gen5 (PCIe 5.0) | 1M+ | <100μs | $300 | etcd, hot databases |
claims.suggested_rewrite: | **0** | NVMe Gen5 (PCIe 5.0) | very high | sub-millisecond | highest | etcd, hot databases |
claims.rationale: The row mixes exact benchmark and pricing figures without a stable source.

claims.claim_text: NVMe Gen4 storage provides 500K+ IOPS, sub-200μs latency, and costs $150/TB.
claims.anchor_text: | **1** | NVMe Gen4 (PCIe 4.0) | 500K+ | <200μs | $150 | App data, Ceph OSD |
claims.suggested_rewrite: | **1** | NVMe Gen4 (PCIe 4.0) | high | sub-millisecond | high | app data, Ceph OSD |
claims.rationale: The row presents volatile benchmark and pricing numbers as facts.

claims.claim_text: Enterprise SATA SSDs provide 50-100K IOPS, 1-5ms latency, and cost $80/TB.
claims.anchor_text: | **2** | SATA SSD (enterprise) | 50-100K | 1-5ms | $80 | Logs, bulk storage |
claims.suggested_rewrite: | **2** | SATA SSD (enterprise) | moderate | low millisecond | medium | logs, bulk storage |
claims.rationale: The row uses uncited benchmark ranges and pricing.

claims.claim_text: 10K/15K RPM SAS HDDs provide 100-200 IOPS, 5-15ms latency, and cost $20/TB.
claims.anchor_text: | **3** | HDD SAS (10K/15K RPM) | 100-200 | 5-15ms | $20 | Backup, cold storage |
claims.suggested_rewrite: | **3** | HDD SAS (10K/15K RPM) | low | higher millisecond | lowest | backup, cold storage |
claims.rationale: The row uses uncited benchmark ranges and pricing.

claims.claim_text: SATA SSDs will cause etcd elections.
claims.anchor_text: - **etcd**: Tier 0 or 1 ONLY (SATA SSD will cause elections).
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **etcd**: Use storage that consistently meets the measured WAL fsync target under load.
claims.rationale: The SATA SSD election statement is overbroad and should be tied to measured fsync latency instead.

claims.claim_text: Ceph OSDs require Tier 1 minimum because SATA SSD limits throughput.
claims.anchor_text: - **Ceph OSD**: Tier 1 minimum (SATA SSD limits throughput).
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Ceph OSD**: Match OSD media to workload throughput and latency requirements, then verify with benchmarks.
claims.rationale: The tier requirement is presented as a universal benchmark rule without a source.

claims.claim_text: Ceph WAL/DB should use a separate high-performance device from OSD data.
claims.rationale: Ceph BlueStore documentation explains DB/WAL device placement, but docs.ceph.com is not allowlisted.

claims.claim_text: Ceph and software-defined local storage should not use hardware RAID and expect raw HBAs in IT mode.
claims.rationale: Ceph hardware guidance is the right source for controller and raw-device recommendations, but the domain is not allowlisted.

claims.claim_text: A 100TB raw Ceph cluster with replication factor 3 yields about 33TB usable and should stay below 70% fill.
claims.anchor_text: A 100TB raw Ceph cluster with a replication factor of 3 yields ~33TB usable. Plan for a 70% maximum fill rate; exceeding this severely impacts rebalancing during node failures.
claims.suggested_rewrite: A Ceph cluster with a replication factor of 3 has roughly one third of its raw capacity available before operational free-space reserves. Keep recovery headroom available so node failures can rebalance without filling the remaining OSDs.
claims.rationale: The one-third calculation is straightforward, but the 70% maximum fill rate is an uncited operational threshold.

claims.claim_text: Dedicated storage nodes are best for clusters above 100 nodes.
claims.span_hint: section: Dedicated Storage Nodes vs Hyper-Converged
claims.anchor_text: - **Best for:** > 100 nodes, high I/O workloads, regulated environments.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Best for:** larger clusters, high I/O workloads, regulated environments.
claims.rationale: The node-count threshold is an uncited rule of thumb.

claims.claim_text: Hyper-converged storage is best for clusters below 50 nodes.
claims.span_hint: section: Dedicated Storage Nodes vs Hyper-Converged
claims.anchor_text: - **Best for:** < 50 nodes, budget-constrained, moderate I/O workloads.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Best for:** smaller clusters, budget-constrained environments, moderate I/O workloads.
claims.rationale: The node-count threshold is an uncited sizing rule.

claims.claim_text: Ceph was started at UC Santa Cruz by Sage Weil in 2004, formalized in a 2007 PhD thesis, became the backbone for most OpenStack deployments, and is now the default on-prem Kubernetes distributed storage via Rook.
claims.anchor_text: - **Ceph was started at UC Santa Cruz** by Sage Weil in 2004 and formalized in his PhD thesis in 2007. It became the storage backbone for most OpenStack deployments and is now the default distributed storage for on-premises Kubernetes via Rook.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Ceph originated as Sage Weil's UC Santa Cruz PhD research** and is now a mature open-source distributed storage system that Rook can orchestrate for Kubernetes.
claims.rationale: The named dates and broad 'most/default' adoption claims need stronger sourcing than the module provides.

claims.claim_text: NVMe drives can fail faster than SATA SSDs under sustained write loads because they have higher write amplification at full speed, and Samsung PM9A3 has much higher DWPD than consumer NVMe.
claims.anchor_text: - **NVMe drives can fail faster under sustained write loads** than SATA SSDs because they have higher write amplification at full speed. Enterprise NVMe drives (like Samsung PM9A3) have much higher endurance (DWPD — Drive Writes Per Day) than consumer NVMe. Always use enterprise-grade drives for Ceph OSDs.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Drive endurance varies by model and workload.** For Ceph OSDs, choose enterprise drives with rated DWPD or TBW appropriate to sustained write-heavy operation.
claims.rationale: The failure comparison and named product endurance claim need vendor datasheets and are too specific to leave uncited.

claims.claim_text: A Samsung PM9A3 provides 1M random read IOPS; a mid-range EMC VNX from 2014 delivered about 200K IOPS from 120 disks; modern on-prem storage can outperform legacy enterprise storage at one-tenth the cost.
claims.anchor_text: - **A single NVMe drive provides more IOPS than an entire SAN array from 10 years ago.** A Samsung PM9A3 (3.84TB) delivers 1M random read IOPS. A mid-range EMC VNX from 2014 delivered ~200K IOPS from 120 spinning disks. Modern on-prem storage can outperform legacy enterprise storage at 1/10th the cost.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Modern NVMe drives can deliver far more random I/O than legacy disk-heavy arrays.** Treat datasheet IOPS as a starting point, then benchmark the exact drives, controllers, and workload profile you plan to run.
claims.rationale: The product comparison, year, IOPS figures, disk count, and cost ratio are uncited benchmark and pricing claims.

claims.claim_text: Kubernetes PersistentVolumes are statically provisioned by default and dynamic provisioning is essential for on-prem.
claims.anchor_text: - **Kubernetes persistent volumes are statically provisioned by default** — you create a PV manually and a PVC claims it. Dynamic provisioning (via StorageClass + CSI driver) is essential for on-prem. Without it, every PV request becomes a manual ticket.
claims.suggested_rewrite: - **Kubernetes supports both static and dynamic PersistentVolume provisioning.** Without a StorageClass and provisioner, PV requests remain a manual administrator workflow.
claims.rationale: The 'by default' and 'essential' framing is overbroad compared with Kubernetes storage documentation.

claims.claim_text: Ceph OSD cgroup limits should be 2 cores plus 4GB per OSD.
claims.anchor_text: Use cgroup limits: `2 cores + 4GB per OSD`
claims.suggested_rewrite: Set explicit CPU and memory limits per OSD based on device count, workload, and benchmark results
claims.rationale: The exact CPU and memory limit is an uncited sizing recommendation.

claims.claim_text: Ceph replication factor 3 tolerates one failure.
claims.rationale: Ceph documentation explains three-replica pools and replica sizing.

claims.claim_text: Dedicated storage nodes are recommended above 100 nodes.
claims.anchor_text: | Ceph on worker nodes at scale | Rebalancing kills application performance | Dedicated storage nodes above 100 nodes |
claims.suggested_rewrite: | Ceph on worker nodes at scale | Rebalancing can hurt application performance | Prefer dedicated storage nodes for larger or high-I/O clusters |
claims.rationale: The exact node threshold is an uncited rule of thumb.

claims.claim_text: Ceph plus PostgreSQL application replication creates 9 copies of every write.
claims.anchor_text: Ceph replicates data (typically 3x) at the block level, and PostgreSQL replicates it again at the application level, resulting in 9 copies of every write across the network.
claims.suggested_rewrite: Ceph replicates data at the block level, and PostgreSQL can replicate it again at the application level, multiplying each write across the network.
claims.rationale: The exact copy count is a back-of-envelope calculation tied to assumptions rather than a cited fact.

claims.claim_text: A replication factor of 3 requires at least 3 OSD nodes because replicas must be placed on distinct nodes.
claims.rationale: Rook's example configuration documentation directly states replication of 3 requires at least three worker nodes, but rook.io is not allowlisted.

claims.claim_text: For production Ceph, 5 or more nodes are highly recommended.
claims.anchor_text: However, for a production environment, 5 or more nodes are highly recommended so that you can tolerate a failure, perform rolling maintenance, and have enough spare capacity to rebalance the data automatically.
claims.suggested_rewrite: However, for a production environment, more than the bare minimum is recommended so that you can tolerate failures, perform rolling maintenance, and keep enough spare capacity for rebalancing.
claims.rationale: The five-node recommendation is an uncited sizing threshold.

claims.claim_text: SATA SSDs generally have 2-10ms fsync latency and can spike beyond 50ms under heavy I/O.
claims.anchor_text: SATA SSDs generally exhibit an fsync latency of 2-10ms, but under heavy I/O load, this can spike beyond 50ms.
claims.suggested_rewrite: SATA SSDs can show higher and more variable fsync latency than NVMe under load.
claims.rationale: The latency range and spike threshold are uncited benchmark values.

claims.claim_text: etcd's default heartbeat interval is 100ms, and slow disk fsync can cause missed heartbeats and leader elections.
claims.rationale: The etcd tuning documentation is the primary source for heartbeat timing and disk-induced heartbeat issues, but etcd.io is not allowlisted.

claims.claim_text: NVMe drives consistently provide sub-millisecond fsync latency for etcd.
claims.anchor_text: The permanent fix is to replace the SATA SSDs with NVMe drives for the etcd data directory (or move etcd to Tier 0/1 storage), as NVMe drives consistently provide sub-millisecond fsync latencies.
claims.suggested_rewrite: The durable fix is to move the etcd data directory to storage that consistently meets the measured WAL fsync target under load.
claims.rationale: The universal sub-millisecond NVMe claim is an uncited benchmark generalization.

further_reading.title: Kubernetes Persistent Volumes
further_reading.why_relevant: Defines PV/PVC lifecycle, access modes, volume modes, reclaim policies, and feature states used throughout the module.

further_reading.title: Kubernetes Storage Classes
further_reading.why_relevant: Explains dynamic provisioning, reclaim policy defaults, volume expansion, and WaitForFirstConsumer binding.

further_reading.title: Kubernetes In-Tree to CSI Migration Status
further_reading.why_relevant: Provides the upstream status and rationale for CSI migration becoming GA.

further_reading.title: Rook: Storage Orchestration for Kubernetes
further_reading.why_relevant: Primary project source for running and operating Ceph through Kubernetes primitives.

further_reading.title: Operating etcd Clusters for Kubernetes
further_reading.why_relevant: Covers why etcd stability is sensitive to disk and network I/O in Kubernetes control planes.

notes: The module contains several likely fabricated or over-precise war-story, benchmark, and sizing claims. It also states OCI image volumes are GA in v1.35, but Kubernetes v1.35 documentation marks image volumes as beta.
